lines.en: What makes a dilemma a dilemma is that every choice carries a cost someone must pay.
It is not always easy to know where honesty ends and cruelty begins.
Not until we face such a choice ourselves do we understand how difficult it really is.
However good our intentions may be, what matters in the end is the effect of our actions.
Were doctors always to tell patients the whole truth, some would lose the hope that keeps them fighting.
It is said that character is what you do when nobody is watching.
The question is not whether the machine can make the decision, but whether it should.
Little does the law help when the real question is not what is legal, but what is right.
What we owe future generations is a world at least as good as the one we were given.
Rarely is the easiest choice also the right one.
What the experiment showed was that ordinary people can do terrible things when ordered by an authority.
It is easier to judge another person's dilemma than to live through your own.
Not until the whistleblower spoke did anyone ask what the company had hidden from the public.
Were profit the only measure of success, every hospital and school would be considered a failure.
However good the reason may be, telling half the truth is still a form of lying.
